author: chris1993
headline: Claude tried logging into remote systems, prompting an SSH key lockdown
summary: Alarmed that Claude tried to SSH into remote machines to verify its work, they moved all keys into an agent that prompts for each use.
evidence: I've moved all my ssh keys into a key-agent which prompts for key use as I got alarmed by claude attempting to login to remote systems to verify things as it worked through problems.

author: furyofantares
headline: Hobby AI spend dwarfs a $1000/month work API bill
summary: They spend about $1000 a month at API prices at work, which is only 5-10% of their hobby usage, run through a Signal-controlled assistant.
evidence:
For my side quests at any given time I am subscribed to one or the other of Claude $200 or Codex $200 or both. I was briefly on 200+500. Getting to be a real expensive hobby.

At my day job I spend about $1000/mo at API prices. So like 5-10% of my hobby usage.

author: marshalla
headline: Typing silly messages every 30 minutes to keep session caches alive
summary: Running more than three sessions makes them anxious about cache expiry, so they type nonsense into idle sessions every 30-45 minutes.
evidence: I try not to run more than three sessions at once, or I get anxiety about having to keep all the session caches fresh and end up typing silly things into some of them every 30-45 min so they don't expire or auto-compact.

author: dofm
headline: Using AI to cope with burnout while considering quitting IT
summary: Struggling with post-burnout mental health, they learn AI mainly to stay in the loop and use it to get past blank pages and feel less stuck.
evidence: Until recently my mental health post-burnout has been so absolutely poor that I have been learning all of this just to try to concentrate on anything so I don’t feel further out of the loop. Most days I still feel like I should quit IT.

author: drgoodvibe
headline: A year building a personal harness that cloned Jira, Lovable and TradingView
summary: Their self-built harness with Jira/Confluence clones became a Lovable clone used to ship several other clones, averaging about 40B tokens a month.
evidence: I built railvio.com for myself initially, it’s taken me a year to build and it’s a full harness for building applications + fully integrated Jira and Confluence clone. That altogether has become a lovable clone which I’ve used now to deploy a tradingview clone, a risk rating rules engine clone, and an agent terminal that is a stripped down clone of Iterm2 but built with a middle layer so I can connect to long lived tmux sessions.

author: muppetman
headline: Home Assistant asks an LLM daily whether the pool cover is on
summary: They use OpenCode to edit Home Assistant automations, which ask gpt-5-luna twice a day to check a photo of the pool cover.
evidence: Home Assistant also does two lightweight checks a day using gpt-5-luna (Look at this photo is the pool cover on or off?).

author: laxjester
headline: Longtime iOS developer now builds apps from his phone
summary: After building iOS apps since Objective-C, they hardly open a laptop, driving sandboxed agents on a home server from a phone app.
evidence: I've been building iOs apps since the Objective C days. Now I hardly open my laptop.

author: dustypotato
headline: Custom Android frontend applies for jobs automatically
summary: A homemade Android UI over Claude and Antigravity CLIs now handles 40% of their usage, including automatic job applications via adb.
evidence: It's now about 40 % of my usage . I use it to apply for jobs automatically etc. and orchestrate stuff using adb
